title: In the admin panel's Your questions, a second reply from the MettleUp team wipes out the first
what: The panel's question history is a hand-kept copy of the member app's rules, marked 'change both', but only the app was changed when the team gained the power to send several replies. The server now sends every reply plus the newest one alone; the panel reads only the newest one and writes it over the earlier reply, so the owner sees just the last reply and loses the earlier ones. No test compares the two copies, unlike the workout-code rules, which have such a test.
expected: The panel keeps and shows every team reply to a question, like the member app, and a test fails when the two copies of the rules drift apart.
how_often: whenever the team replies twice to one question
fix_line: Bring the panel's question rules up to the app's (keep every reply) and add a test that compares the two copies

title: Small rules are written twice in the panel's logic (month of a day, a member's mobile number)
what: The growth report has its own 'month of a day' beside the shared date rules' identical one, and the message audience has its own mobile-number reader (Indian 10 digits only) beside the shared phone reader the import and forms use. Today they agree, but a change to one copy will not reach the other.
expected: One rule for each: the growth report uses the shared month rule and the audience uses the shared phone reader.
how_often: on the next change to either rule
fix_line: Point both places at the shared rule and delete the copies
